title: What is Fabric IQ? - Microsoft Fabric | Microsoft Learn
summary: Microsoft Learn's conceptual introduction to Fabric IQ, the new Fabric workload that turns raw OneLake data into shared business meaning (via semantic models and an ontology item) so that people and AI agents can reason about customers, shipments, and other business concepts consistently. It also positions Fabric IQ inside the broader 'Microsoft IQ' enterprise-intelligence layer alongside Work IQ, Foundry IQ, and Web IQ, and inventories the Fabric items that make up the IQ (preview) workload.
audience: Architects and platform owners evaluating how to ground Copilot/agent experiences in consistent business semantics, and BI teams deciding whether to extend existing Power BI semantic models into an ontology.
why_it_matters: Fabric IQ is brand new (preview) and currently has no claims in the knowledge base, which blocks /publish-topic for the AI & APIs section. This source establishes the baseline conceptual (L1) claims needed before deeper practitioner content on ontology, data agents, and operations agents can be layered in.
takeaways: Fabric IQ is one of four pillars of 'Microsoft IQ' (with Work IQ, Foundry IQ, Web IQ), and its specific job is supplying business-entity and data context.
Two Fabric items anchor Fabric IQ: the existing Power BI semantic model (curated analytics layer) and the new ontology (preview) item (business vocabulary, relationships, rules, actions).
Ontologies can be generated/aligned directly from existing semantic models, so production BI investments can bootstrap the ontology rather than starting from scratch.

The IQ (preview) workload bundles several items beyond ontology and semantic model: Plan (preview), Graph, Data agent, and Operations agent (preview) — most of which are shared with other Fabric workloads.
OneLake remains the unifying data substrate underneath Fabric IQ even though it is not formally listed as an IQ workload item.

claims.text: Fabric IQ is part of Microsoft IQ, an enterprise intelligence layer that also includes Work IQ (employee work context), Foundry IQ (organizational policy/document context), and Web IQ (web context); Fabric IQ's role is business-entity and data context.

Fabric IQ brings three layers of business context into Microsoft IQ — unified data, business intelligence, and operational intelligence — delivered through two core Fabric items: the ontology (preview) and the semantic model.

OneLake underlies Fabric IQ as the unifying layer across clouds and on-premises sources, using shortcuts, mirroring, and the OneLake catalog so the same governed data grounds semantic models, ontologies, and agents.

Ontologies in Fabric IQ can be generated or aligned directly from Power BI semantic models already in production, so business terms and KPIs stay consistent across reports, agents, and applications instead of being redefined per experience.

An ontology (preview) item defines core business entities, relationships, properties, rules, and actions, and exposes a natural-language query layer (NL2Ontology) that converts business questions into structured queries.

Without a shared ontology layer, AI systems are described as unfit for high-stakes decisions because every business question otherwise requires manual translation by a domain expert from raw tables/schemas into business concepts.

Fabric IQ's stated benefits are cross-domain reasoning via graph relationship traversal (e.g., chaining Order to Shipment to sensor to a cold-chain breach), faster onboarding because business concepts are declared once, and governance from enforcing consistent definitions across teams.

The IQ (preview) workload in Fabric groups several items beyond ontology and semantic model: Plan (preview) for planning/forecasting, Graph for storing and traversing connected data, Data agent for natural-language Q&A, and Operations agent (preview) for monitoring live data and triggering governed actions.

A Fabric data agent is described as a virtual analyst connected to Fabric data sources that answers natural-language questions for a specific domain, grounded in semantic models and ontologies, and publishable across Microsoft 365, Foundry, Copilot Studio, and custom apps.

An operations agent (preview) is an AI agent that reasons across business concepts to monitor real-time data, detect anomalies, and recommend or trigger governed business actions; it is shared between the IQ and Real-Time Intelligence workloads.

Fabric items can belong to multiple workloads simultaneously — for example, the semantic model item is shared with the Power BI workload, and Graph and the operations agent are shared with the Real-Time Intelligence workload.
OneLake is not formally listed as an item inside the IQ (preview) workload, but every item in that workload relies on and interacts natively with OneLake data tables.
